name: Lighting
simple: Lighting controls the look of the whole world's light: the time of day, how bright the sun is, the color of shadows, and fog. You can also put a Sky, an Atmosphere, and effects like Bloom or Blur inside it. Changing Lighting can make your game feel sunny, spooky, or like a sunset.
analogy: Lighting is like the light switches, dimmer, and window blinds for your whole world. Turn the clock to night and the sun goes down; add fog and the far-away things fade into mist.
whenToUse: Make a day and night cycle by changing the time.
Set the mood: dark and foggy for horror, bright and colorful for an obby.
Hold Sky, Atmosphere, and post-processing effects like BloomEffect or ColorCorrectionEffect.
where: A service on both server and client. Get it with `game:GetService("Lighting")`. Changes made by a server Script are seen by everyone; changes made in a LocalScript are seen only by that player.

terms.service: A special built-in object at the top of the game. Get one with `game:GetService("Name")`.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green, and blue amounts. `Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0)` is red.
terms.ambient light: Soft light that fills everything, even places the sun cannot reach directly. It decides how dark shadows are.
terms.fog: A haze that makes far-away things fade into a color.
terms.exposure: How bright the whole picture is made, like a camera letting in more or less light.
terms.specular: Shiny highlights and reflections on smooth surfaces.
terms.latitude: How far north or south on Earth a place is. It changes the sun's path in the sky.
terms.post-processing effect: A filter applied to the whole picture after it is drawn, like blur or extra glow.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something newer.

examples.title: Day and night cycle
examples.code:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")

-- One full day takes 4 minutes (240 seconds)
local secondsPerDay = 240

while true do
	-- ClockTime goes from 0 to 24 (hours). Move it forward a little each step.
	Lighting.ClockTime = (Lighting.ClockTime + 24 / secondsPerDay * 0.1) % 24
	task.wait(0.1)
end
explain: ClockTime is the hour of the day, from 0 (midnight) to 24. 14 means 2 PM.
Every 0.1 seconds we add a tiny bit of time. 24 hours spread over 240 seconds is 0.1 hours per second.
`% 24` wraps it back to 0 after midnight, so the cycle repeats forever.

examples.title: Spooky fog
examples.code:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")

Lighting.ClockTime = 0                          -- midnight
Lighting.FogColor = Color3.fromRGB(40, 40, 50)  -- dark gray-blue
Lighting.FogStart = 0                           -- fog starts right at the camera
Lighting.FogEnd = 80                            -- fully foggy 80 studs away
explain: The time is set to midnight.
Fog begins at 0 studs from the camera and becomes completely solid at 80 studs, so you can barely see far.
If Lighting has an Atmosphere inside, these fog settings are hidden; use the Atmosphere instead.

gotchas: Fog settings stop working when an Atmosphere object is inside Lighting. Use the Atmosphere's Density and Haze instead.
Time does not move on its own. You need a script (like the day/night example) to change it.
Changes from a LocalScript only show for that player, which is useful for things like a personal night-vision effect.

Lighting.Ambient.simple: The color of light in places the sun cannot reach, like indoors or under a roof. Default is black (0, 0, 0). Brighter colors make those shadowy places lighter.
Lighting.Ambient.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
Lighting.Ambient = Color3.fromRGB(70, 70, 70) -- lighter indoor areas

Lighting.Brightness.simple: How strong the sun or moon light is. Higher numbers make sunlit areas brighter.

Lighting.ClockTime.simple: The time of day as a number of hours, from 0 to 24. 6 is sunrise-ish, 12 is noon, 18 is evening, 0 is midnight. It only changes if a script changes it.

Lighting.ColorShift_Bottom.simple: A color tint added to the sides of parts facing AWAY from the sun or moon.
Lighting.ColorShift_Bottom.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
Lighting.ColorShift_Bottom = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 80) -- bluish undersides

Lighting.ColorShift_Top.simple: A color tint added to the sides of parts facing TOWARD the sun or moon. Orange looks like a warm sunset.
Lighting.ColorShift_Top.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
Lighting.ColorShift_Top = Color3.fromRGB(255, 150, 50) -- warm sunlight

Lighting.EnvironmentDiffuseScale.simple: How much soft light comes from the sky itself, from 0 to 1. Unlike Ambient, it changes with the sky and the time of day.

Lighting.EnvironmentSpecularScale.simple: How much smooth and metal surfaces reflect the sky around them, from 0 to 1. Makes metal look more real.

Lighting.ExposureCompensation.simple: Brightens or darkens the whole picture, from -5 to 5. 1 is twice as bright, -1 is half as bright, 0 is normal.
Lighting.ExposureCompensation.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
Lighting.ExposureCompensation = -1 -- a darker scene

Lighting.ExtendLightRangeTo120.simple: Unused hidden setting. Lights are always limited to a range of 120 studs anyway.

Lighting.FogEnd.simple: How far from the camera, in studs, the fog becomes completely solid. Smaller numbers mean thicker fog.

Lighting.FogStart.simple: How far from the camera, in studs, the fog starts to appear.

Lighting.GeographicLatitude.simple: Pretends your world is at a place on Earth this many degrees north or south. It changes the sun's path across the sky at each time of day.
Lighting.GeographicLatitude.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
Lighting.GeographicLatitude = 60 -- far north: lower sun

Lighting.GlobalShadows.simple: If true, the sun and moon cast shadows, and sheltered areas get the darker Ambient color.

Lighting.LightingStyle.simple: The overall art style of the light: Soft (more cartoony) or Realistic (more like real life).

Lighting.OutdoorAmbient.simple: The color of soft fill light outdoors. Default is gray (127, 127, 127). Whiter makes outside look brighter.

Lighting.Outlines.simple: Old — outlines on parts are no longer drawn.

Lighting.PrioritizeLightingQuality.simple: On slower devices, decides what to lower first: if true, keep nice lighting and shadows up close and draw less far away; if false, keep the view distance and simplify lighting.

Lighting.ShadowColor.simple: Old — no longer used. Use `Ambient` to change shadow color.

Lighting.ShadowSoftness.simple: How blurry shadow edges are, from 0 (sharp) to 1 (very soft). Default 0.2. Only works with the newer lighting modes on devices that support them.

Lighting.Technology.simple: Old — set the lighting mode in Studio, and use `LightingStyle` and `PrioritizeLightingQuality` instead.

Lighting.TimeOfDay.simple: The time of day as text on a 24-hour clock, like "14:00:00" for 2 PM or "21:30:00" for 9:30 PM. Changing it also changes ClockTime.

Lighting:GetMinutesAfterMidnight.simple: Gives how many minutes past midnight the lighting clock is. About ClockTime times 60, so 2 PM gives 840.

Lighting:GetMoonDirection.simple: Gives a direction (a Vector3 of length 1) pointing from the center of the world toward the moon. It still points at the moon even when the moon is below the horizon.

Lighting:GetSunDirection.simple: Gives a direction (a Vector3 of length 1) pointing from the center of the world toward the sun. If its Y is below 0, the sun has set.
Lighting:GetSunDirection.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
if Lighting:GetSunDirection().Y < 0 then
	print("It is night")
end

Lighting:SetMinutesAfterMidnight.simple: Sets the time of day using minutes after midnight, so you can use plain numbers. 720 is noon, 1080 is 6 PM.

Lighting.LightingChanged.simple: Fires when a Lighting setting changes or a Sky is added or removed. It gives true if the change was about the sky.
Lighting.LightingChanged.example:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
Lighting.LightingChanged:Connect(function(skyChanged)
	print("Lighting changed. Sky changed?", skyChanged)
end)
Lighting.LightingChanged.gotcha: It does not fire for fog or GlobalShadows changes. Use `GetPropertyChangedSignal` for those.
